Exactly. What we're having happen right now is exactly what our economic system is supposed to stop from happening which is why the Fed is freaking out. The whole goal of our economy is to keep money flowing. The idea is somebody gets rich and then in order to get even richer they invest in other people who are in the process of getting rich. This then iterates upward with more and more money being thrown around and invested helping everybody rise up. This is the basic idea behind supply side economics.

Now a big catalyst in this system is inflation. When we have deflation if somebody has an enormous amount of money that money becomes worth even more with them doing nothing but tucking it under their mattress. Investments invariably have some degree of risk yet deflation is risk free guaranteed profit. Inflation works the exact opposite. If you have 10 billion dollars tucked away then 2% of inflation means you're going to lose $200 million next year if you don't do something - like invest it.

So to avoid hoarding and encourage investment the Fed pushes for inflation through a wide array of methods. The most recent was the idea of setting the Fed rates to negative. That doesn't mean your bank account has a negative interest rate but rather that the Fed sets their lending rate at negative - people banks are literally paid money to borrow. The idea here again being that they'll borrow a ton of money, start aggressively dumping it into the economy, and at the same time as we see economic growth - we also see inflation resulting in even more investing and blah blah happily ever after.

But like you've said right now we're in a pretty terrible situation. Jobs growth is terrible with an increasing number of the jobs that are coming out being go nowhere McJobs, the Fed can't get inflation up, and the wealthy are increasingly just hoarding.

I think the problem is probably far more complex than people are giving credit for. A finite good-backed currency (such as a gold standard) simply doesn't work. But I think we're also seeing that a currency based on a debt-investment cycle such as current system also doesn't work. Ultimately I think we're going to see something like a universal basic income in the longrun (the St Louis Fed was already investigating the viability and benefits of a basic income at the end of last year), but this is going to be such a revolutionary change in the US socioeconomic system that I imagine we're going to look for every single possible alternative before that.
